[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:06. The shot opens on a wide across dusty olive heather at the raw ring of flung yellow sand round the crater on a hot bright afternoon, one continuous grey streamer of smoke standing straight up out of it in the air, the heath running away flat to low pines, and the raw sand lying and bare inside its ring. The camera is on the heath at a standing man's eye, a 35mm lens. A hard high sun stands at the RIGHT. At the first frame Dusty olive heather fills the BOTTOM third of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, with the shallow ditch and its thrown-up spoil running across the BOTTOM LEFT. The raw ring of flung yellow sand runs across the CENTRE, a tenth of the height of the frame, and the single grey streamer of smoke stands straight up out of it at the CENTRE into the TOP third. Low pines close the horizon behind the ring and a pale hot sky fills the TOP third. The shot is inside this place: the sand-pits on Horsell Common on a hot bright afternoon in 1894: the raw ring of flung yellow sand round the crater, a single continuous streamer of grey smoke standing straight up out of it in the air, knee-deep heather and dark furze running away flat to a horizon of low pines. The camera rises from the heather with small amplitude until the whole ring of sand and the standing streamer of smoke are inside the picture as the streamer goes on rising straight up out of the pit, from 00:00 to 00:03. At 00:03 the heather goes on stirring in the hot air, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:06 the camera is riseing through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
